title: Most games reward you for building the ultimate defense. Mine penalizes you: double your DPS and the boss takes 2.3× longer to die. Claude agents tuned the formula. Bug or feature?
author: Curious_Weight_1193
selftext:
Most games reward you for building the ultimate defense. Mine penalizes you: double your DPS and the boss takes 2.3× longer to die. Claude agents tuned the formula. Bug or feature?

# Body

HEARTHWATCH is a neon tower defense where the map tears open mid-battle. In a run, levels, cards, items and branches multiply, and a good player ends up about 6× stronger than a fixed wave schedule expects. So every enemy uses this formula:

    HP    = base × D(w) × RB × difficulty
    D(w)  = 1 + 0.06·(w−1)
    ref   = 45 + 10·(w−1)                  // DPS I expect at wave w
    ratio = (tower DPS + unspent Ember) / ref
    RB    = 1 + K·max(0, ratio − 1)        // K = 0.62 normal, 3.6 boss
    pack  = 1 + ⌊2·(ratio − 1)⌋, max 5      // same-kind enemies spawn together
    difficulty: easy 0.8 · normal 1.0 · hard 1.35

None of these numbers were hand-tuned. A small team of Claude agents (in Claude Code) built a headless sim, swept the knobs, and found exploits along the way:

* **Exploit:** hoarding Ember made waves easier. Fixed: unspent Ember now counts as power.
* **Bug:** packs spawned stacked on one pixel. Fixed.
* **Desync:** the sim ramps K late in the game, but the game never reads that knob. Still open.

**The dilemma:** time-to-kill scales with (1 + K(r−1)) / r. When K > 1 it flips. At 2× DPS, normal enemies die 19% faster, but bosses take 2.3× longer. If getting stronger makes the boss slower, the optimal play is to *not* upgrade, which is Oblivion's leveling problem all over again.

Two fixes I'm weighing:

* **A:** scale the boss's mechanics (shields, speed bursts, summons) instead of its HP.
* **B:** a diminishing penalty, RB = r\^0.77. Then 2× DPS always kills \~15% faster, never slower.

So what would you do: cap the scaling and let god-tier builds melt the boss in 2 seconds, or keep the penalty so the run stays tense? Which formula would you pick?

Steam: [https://store.steampowered.com/app/5078340/HEARTHWATCH/](https://store.steampowered.com/app/5078340/HEARTHWATCH/)

comments.author: joshbuildsstuff
comments.body:
This feels like a lot of work, when you could of just given the boss more health to begin with 🤷‍♂️

If you want it to be a power fantasy type game then certain builds need to destroy the bosses fast as they get stronger.  If your boss outscales your DPS increase than the player can never hit any real power spike during boss fights.

replies.author: Curious_Weight_1193
replies.body: hmm... You're right about the power spike, and honestly that's the strongest argument for option B: with K above 1 a stronger build can never feel strnger against a boss, which kills the fantasy. The catch with just raising base HP is the spread, by late game player DPS varies about 6x between builds, so any flat number is either a wall for weaker builds or a speed bump for strong ones. So I'm leaning towards keeping some scaling but tapering it , so a 2x build always kills noticeably faster.

replies.author: joshbuildsstuff
replies.body: 6x feels like a lot for a tower defense game and probably why your balancing is so hard, and not all builds should be able to beat the same bosses at that level of difference.  If your goal is to provide different play styles like projectiles vs. chip vs. lightning, etc. I would get your builds closer together in terms of DPS.  Of figure out how to make this more of a progression type game where they continuously upgrade to the better builds.
